title: Ubiquiti UniFi USW-Pro-XG-10-PoE Review A Sweet 10GbE Switch
gist: ServeTheHome's hardware-overview review of Ubiquiti's new $699 USW-Pro-XG-10-PoE 10GbE switch, an upgrade to the $499 8-port model with two more ports, higher PoE power budget, and a 1U rack form factor versus the prior desktop design.

insights.claim: The Ubiquiti UniFi USW-Pro-XG-10-PoE is priced at $699, a notable step up from the $499 price of the lower-end USW-Pro-XG-8-PoE it upgrades from, in exchange for more ports and higher PoE power budget.
insights.speaker: Rohit Kumar
insights.so_what: A 40% price step-up ($499 to $699) for two extra 10GbE ports plus more PoE budget gives buyers and competitors a concrete per-port cost benchmark for prosumer/SMB 10GbE PoE switching, relevant to assessing Ubiquiti's pricing strategy versus rivals like TP-Link, MikroTik, and Netgear in this segment.
insights.quote: At the time of this review, this is a $699 device, a notable increase over the $499 lower-end model.

insights.claim: The USW-Pro-XG-10-PoE switches from the desktop form factor of the 8-port model to a full 1U rackmount form factor, a design change described as 'night and day' different.
insights.speaker: Rohit Kumar
insights.so_what: The shift to a proper 1U rack form factor signals Ubiquiti is positioning this SKU more toward small-business/prosumer server-room deployments rather than desk-side home-lab use, widening its addressable market versus the entry-level model.
insights.quote: While the '8' was more of a desktop form factor, this is a 1U form factor switch.

insights.claim: Despite being marketed as a 10-port switch, the device actually has 12 usable ports: ten 10GBase-T copper ports plus two SFP+ 10Gbps fiber ports.
insights.speaker: Rohit Kumar
insights.so_what: The naming understates true port count (12 vs. advertised 10), a useful spec correction for buyers comparing per-port cost against competing 10GbE switches that advertise total port counts more literally.
insights.quote: Calling this a 10-port switch is a bit misleading, since it has two SFP+ 10Gbps ports, so it actually has 12 ports.

insights.claim: The ten 10GBase-T ports support Ubiquiti's Etherlighting and PoE+++ (802.3bt Type 4 Class 8) power delivery, offering two more ports and better PoE capability than the 8-port predecessor model.
insights.speaker: Rohit Kumar
insights.so_what: 802.3bt Type 4 Class 8 is the highest current PoE power tier, indicating this switch targets high-power PoE devices (e.g., PTZ cameras, WiFi 7 APs) beyond what typical PoE+ switches support — a relevant spec for network infrastructure buyers scaling power-hungry edge devices.
insights.quote: These support Ubiquiti’s Etherlighting and PoE+++ modes, which provide 802.3bt Type 4 Class 8 power delivery.

insights.claim: The switch includes a 1.3-inch touchscreen status display with AR switch management, four rear fans, both DC (for Ubiquiti's UPS Connect power accessories) and AC power inputs, a power-cable safety lock, rack ears, and an accessory pack (cage nuts, screws, rubber feet for desk mounting).
insights.speaker: Rohit Kumar
insights.so_what: Minor build-quality/feature checklist (touchscreen, dual power input, cable lock) relevant mainly to prosumer buyers evaluating fit and finish versus competing 10GbE PoE switches; not a strategic signal.
